explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly compares GPT-4 judgments against human expert ratings on a subset of 16 dialogues, reporting win/loss rates and discussing correlation verification.

prompts.notes: Full prompts shown in appendix figures, including detailed evaluation criteria and response format specifications.

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: high agreement on subset selection problem

guidelines.notes: Detailed annotator instructions shown in §J with 4-point Likert scale definitions for each criterion.

sample_size.notes: Validated on subset of 16 dialogues from test set

quantitative_scores.notes: GPT-4 can match both controlled and crowdsourced human preferences well according to cited prior work (Zheng et al., 2023)

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: matching controlled and crowdsourced human preferences

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 judgments show strong correlation with human expert ratings, with GPT-4-based writers achieving high win rates (82.7-93.8%) on key criteria compared to baselines.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluation focused on content-based criteria while human evaluation included additional qualitative aspects like coherence, violation checking, and engagingness.
